title: Nearest Pair of Two Words
statement:
You get a list of words and two different words first and second, both of which occur somewhere in the list, possibly many times.

Return the smallest distance |i − j| between an index i where first occurs and an index j where second occurs.

examples.why: The first "map" and first "set" are 3 apart, but the later pair at indexes 5 and 6 is only 1 apart.
The distance is absolute: second may come before first in the list.
Several pairs are 1 apart. Only the distance is returned, not the positions.

constraints: first ≠ second, and both appear in words
hints: Comparing every occurrence of first with every occurrence of second works. Which comparisons can never win?
For an occurrence of second, the only occurrence of first worth checking on its left is the nearest one, which is the most recent one you passed.
Walk once, remembering the latest index of each word. Whenever you see either word and the other has been seen, compare the gap.

explain.intuition:
Walk the list left to right and think about pairs that end at the current index. If the current word is second, the best partner on its left is the most recent first; any older one is further away. The same holds the other way around.

So keep only two numbers: the last index of first and the last index of second. Each time you meet one of them, update its index and compare with the other's. Every closest pair is checked when you reach its right end.
steps: For each index i: if words[i] is first, set lastFirst = i; if it is second, set lastSecond = i.
If both are set, update best with |lastFirst − lastSecond|.
pitfalls: Comparing only the first occurrence of each word, which fails on the first example.
Assuming first always comes before second and returning a negative distance.
Collecting all positions and comparing every pair, which is O(n²) when both words are frequent.

solutions.title: Compare every pair of positions
solutions.idea: Collect the positions of both words and try every combination.

solutions.title: One pass with the latest positions
solutions.idea: Remember the most recent index of each word; every time one of them appears, compare with the other.

followups: The same list is queried many times with different word pairs. What would you precompute? (Hint: sorted position lists and a merge.)
first and second may be the same word. What changes?
